messages:
maya: Heads-up — bringing a community model into triage: 'Whitestone-11B' (weights from GH repo). License header says CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 and no clear dataset provenance. Want a quick compliance read before we start quant/bench.
liam-legal: ND (no derivatives) + NC (non-commercial) flags are immediate red flags for hosting or offering via API. Quantization and pruning are transformations — could be considered derivatives. Do we have the full license text and contact info for maintainer?
maya: attaching snippet from repo README: ```License: CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0\nTrained on mixed-crawl + curated corpora (see data_manifest.json)``` — no author email in repo.
anya-ml: From past precedence: CC-BY-NC-ND usually prevents us from serving model weights or providing modified binaries. We can still run experiments locally for internal evaluation if access is limited, but shipping a quantized artifact to users = no-go without permission.
sam-platform: @liam-legal noted. Operationally we can isolate experiments in a private Dedicated pool or air-gapped box. If legal approves internal evals only, we should require: KMS for keys, strict ACLs, no external backups, and audit logging.
liam-legal: Agreed. Action items: 1) get full license file and any contributor agreement, 2) request written permission from rights holder for transformations (quant/prune) and for commercial/hosted usage, 3) run dataset provenance check for personal data or licensed third-party corpora.
nora-qa: For the eval plan: we should run a small regression sweep before/after quant: eval suite (SQuAD-like, summarization subset, safety prompts). If we run quant locally, tag artifacts as "for-internal-eval-only" and keep hashes. Also keep prompt seeds used for quality comparisons.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: spun up ephemeral stack "ci-whitestone-2260123456" in prod-vpc-priv for private evals. Stack ID: st-0a1b2c3d
anya-ml: Proposed compliance checklist (short): - confirm license file + owner contact - confirm dataset provenance & export control risk - written permission for derivative/transformations OR treat as eval-only - host only in private Dedicated/VPC with KMS & audit - block any public API exposure or redistribution - run PII scrub on eval prompts/results
liam-legal: Also check export control regs (EAR) and open-source exemptions — model size + capabilities might trigger extra review. I'll loop in export-control team if maintainer cannot provide provenance.
maya: I'll open an intake ticket with repo links, attach our checklist, and try to find maintainer contact. Will hold off on public bring-up until we have written permission. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
sam-platform: Noted — tagging ops to ensure the ephemeral stack is fenced: policy "no-egress" enforced.
maya: quick note — if maintainer grants permission for quant only but forbids redistribution, we can still run quantized runtime in Dedicated and only expose through internal eval dashboards. Will document permissions precisely.
liam-legal: Good. If we get permission, we need a short license addendum (email ok) that explicitly allows transformations and hosting scope. Keep me posted.
maya: Will do. Closing loop here after intake ticket.
